title: Structured Debriefing and Institutional Trust After a Mass-Casualty Simulation
official: Impact of a Structured Post-Simulation Debriefing on Institutional Trust After a Mass-Casualty Incident Exercise: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: This single-center, randomized, parallel-group trial evaluates whether adding a structured psychological and organizational support module to the standard technical debriefing via the PEARLS method after a full-scale hospital mass-casualty incident simulation increases healthcare professionals' confidence in their institution's ability to respond to a mass-casualty incident. Adult hospital professionals with an operational role in the exercise will complete a baseline questionnaire immediately after the exercise and before allocation. Participants will then be randomized 1:1 to standard debriefing control module or to standard debriefing plus a structured psychological and organizational support module. The primary outcome is the post-debriefing institutional confidence score, calculated as the mean of three 7-point Likert items and analyzed with adjustment for the pre-debriefing score.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* adult hospital professional with an operational role during the exercise
* study information received
* voluntary agreement to participate

Exclusion Criteria:

* actors or standardized patients playing victims
* evaluators, organizers, or facilitators without an operational role in the scenario
* refusal to participate in the study
